title: Diversity in the Living World
seo_title: Diversity in the Living World Class 6 Science Worksheet (NCERT Curiosity Ch 2)
standard_code: Class 6, Curiosity Chapter 2: Diversity in the Living World
standard_text: Diversity in plants and animals; grouping plants as herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers and creepers; leaf venation and types of roots; habitats and adaptations of animals and plants; conserving biodiversity (summary of NCERT Curiosity Chapter 2).
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 6 Science worksheets for NCERT Curiosity Chapter 2: herbs, shrubs, trees, climbers and creepers, leaf venation and roots, habitats and adaptations, and biodiversity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Living things are grouped by their features.
key_sub: Parallel veins go with fibrous roots; net-like veins with a taproot.
body_html:
How to think about it

Plants can be grouped by their stems: herbs have soft green stems, shrubs have woody stems branching near the ground, trees have a thick trunk, and climbers and creepers have weak stems. Leaves with net-like (reticulate) venation usually go with a taproot; leaves with parallel venation go with fibrous roots.

Animals and plants have adaptations that help them live in their habitats: a camel in the desert, a fish in water, a yak in cold mountains. The great variety of life is called biodiversity, and we must protect it.

Example

Wheat leaves have parallel veins. Which roots?

parallel venation goes with fibrous roots

Answer: fibrous roots

Example

A rose plant has a woody stem branching near the ground. It is…

medium-sized, woody

Answer: a shrub

Common mistakes

  • Calling a weak-stemmed plant that climbs a creeper.
  • Thinking all plants have a taproot.
  • Calling a dolphin a fish.

faq.q: What is the difference between a climber and a creeper?
faq.a: Both have weak stems; a climber climbs up a support, while a creeper spreads along the ground.

faq.q: Why does a camel have long legs?
faq.a: They keep its body away from the hot desert sand.
